links.outcome: Share of auto-generated reference answers judged defective by physician adjudication
links.effect: Physicians identified 56 percent of auto-generated reference answers as defective; NLP-pipeline clinical-QA benchmarks need physician adjudication to be usable.
links.quote: Physician adjudication identified 56 percent of auto-generated reference answers as defective, a methodological finding indicating that NLP-pipeline clinical-QA benchmarks require physician adjudication to be usable.

links.outcome: Accuracy of assertion-aware knowledge-graph retrieval grounding versus LLM-alone baseline on clinical QA
links.effect: Author-blind primary endpoint +22.0 percentage points (95% Newcombe CI +5.1 to +31.5, p=0.0192); intent-aware KG-RAG over dense-RAG baseline +8.84 pp (p=1.79e-3).
links.quote: The author-blind primary endpoint, leave-author-out paired exact McNemar on 50 unanimous-strict items rated by two external physicians, yields +22.0 percentage points (95 percent Newcombe CI [+5.1, +31.5], p=0.0192).

unlisted_practices: Assertion-aware (negation, temporality, family-vs-patient attribution) labeling of EHR facts before retrieval
Intent-aware routing of retrieval by question type

screen.reason: Empirically benchmarks RAG retrieval safeguards (assertion and temporality-aware knowledge graph routing vs baseline dense RAG) across multiple LLMs for EHR question answering.
